title: A folder, a manifest, and some Lua.
body: A WoW addon is a folder inside Interface/AddOns. The game reads its table-of-contents file first, then loads the files listed there from top to bottom.

files.label: MyFirstAddon.toc
files.title: MyFirstAddon.toc
files.body: The TOC tells WoW what your addon is called, which game interface it supports, and which files to load.
files.code:
## Interface: {{interface}}
## Title: My First Addon
## Notes: Learning addon basics
## Author: Your Name
## Version: 0.1.0

MyFirstAddon.lua
files.note: If one Lua file depends on another, list the dependency first so it is available when later files load.

files.label: MyFirstAddon.lua
files.title: MyFirstAddon.lua
files.body: Lua files contain your addon's behavior: listening for events, calling WoW APIs, storing data, and changing the interface.
files.code:
local addonName = ...

local frame = CreateFrame("Frame")
frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LOGIN")

frame:SetScript("OnEvent", function()
  print(addonName .. " is ready!")
end)
files.note: One file is enough for a first addon. Split code into modules only when each file has a clear responsibility.

files.label: MyFirstAddon.xml
files.title: MyFirstAddon.xml
files.body: XML can declare frames and visual templates. Many modern addons create their interface directly in Lua, so this file is optional.
files.note: Start with Lua unless a guide or an existing Blizzard template gives you a clear reason to use XML.

files.label: SavedVariables
files.title: SavedVariables
files.body: SavedVariables are Lua tables named in the TOC. WoW saves them when you log out or reload and restores them next time.
files.note: Do not edit the generated SavedVariables file while the game is running. Change the table through your addon code instead.

concepts.title: Events
concepts.body: Notifications from the game—such as login, entering combat, or receiving loot—that your Lua code can listen for.

concepts.title: Frames
concepts.body: The building blocks of the interface. Frames can display content, receive events, and contain buttons, text, or textures.

concepts.title: SavedVariables
concepts.body: Tables WoW writes to disk when you log out or reload, allowing your addon to remember settings.

concepts.title: Slash commands
concepts.body: Chat commands such as /hello that give your addon a quick, friendly way to accept input.
